To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a patient presenting a germline TP55346stop/R72P mutation had an impaired response to DNA-damaging agents in fibroblasts.

the proband's TP53Arg72P/TP53stop146 heterozygous cells were not as efficient in causing cell arrest after DNA damage as the control cells and the cells of her mother carrying the TP53Arg 72Pro polymorphism only.

the proband's heteroallelic fibroblasts, which carried the TP53Arg146Stop and TP53Arg72pro polymorphisms, were impaired in their response to DNA damage, which could be related to a diminished TP53 pathway activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with

an in vitro analysis of a TP53stop146 mutant cell model, which could be used to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the LFS phenotype and the role played by the TP53ArgPro72 polymorphism in the TP53 pathway.
the identification of a novel germline TP53346 mutation in a patient with LFS.
a new TP53 nonsense mutation, TP53stop146, in a patient who developed five malignant tumors and one benign meningioma and who carries the TP53ArgPro polymorphism in her second allele.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TP53stop146 mutation in the Li-Fraumenian proband was associated with a disruption in TP53 pathway and a diminished response to DNA damage.
the proband's heterodimer TP53stop146/TP53Arg72Pro was not as efficient as TP53Arg72/Arg72 in response to DNA-damage-induced apoptosis.

the proband's heterologous fibroblast cells are not able to respond to DNA damage as efficiently as the control fibroblastic cells, which could contribute to the high incidence of tumors in the proband.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heterozygous TP53346/R72P fiboblasts are impaired in their ability to respond to DNA damage, and this may be a consequence of diminished TP21 levels.

the TP53stop146 mutation in the LFS family described in the present work is associated with a loss of function of the p53 protein, which may be responsible for the development of multiple tumors in this patient.
the proband's fibroblasts present a diminished response to DNA damage, which may contribute to the development of cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TP53Arg72pro polymorphism is not associated with a higher cancer risk and may not be a risk factor for cancer.
the TP53ArgPro72 variant is a risk factor for cancer development, but it does not confer the same risk as the germline nonsense TP53 mutation.
the TP53stop146 polymorphism is associated with a defective TP53 function, which is not compensated for by the TP53ArgPro polymorphism.
